units: painted: whole pixels at the quality, rows from the bottom; overlay: points; scale: device px per point; offset: device px; lines: whole device px. Every rational is [numerator, denominator]
notes: guardNeeded and guardOn describe rule 1's route in doubles (the share, the draw map at rotation 0, the clip, the transform as given and flipped with K = 100000), and the lands-on-a-line-* rows are searched on it, four per edge each way at 3× and at 2×. Rows: turn-* (the fill in shares of the page as displayed through the draw map, at each turn on an offset crop, with the identity and the planted fault of the turn left out of the fill's map); seeded2x-* and lands-on-a-line-2x-* (a 2× device); a4-150-last-lines; read-the-join-150 and its comparison; rule3-* (rule 3's count rows). The quarter-turn rows (quarter-*): inputs.transform {a, b, c, d, tx, ty} maps (x, y) to (a·x + c·y + tx, b·x + d·y + ty); expected.deviceLines are the device bounding box's lines, and rectExact the rectangle mapped back through the inverse. Expected values are exact (rational). Properties over the stream: the drawn fill holds the true rectangle; it exceeds it by under one device pixel a side; equal inputs give equal outputs. A float implementation needs a guard: an edge whose true device value is a whole number can land a hair off it in doubles, and floor or ceil then pushes the line a whole device pixel out. Rows whose guardNeeded is true are the ones plain doubles get wrong. The reference counts a value within 1e-9 (relative) of a whole number as that number; that is safe while every true value off a line lies further than 1e-9 from it, which the table's rationals guarantee.
